Oxytocin is a cyclic peptide with the sequence CYIQNCPLG–NH₂ and a Cys1–Cys6 disulfide. Tyr2 sits deep in the receptor pocket.

Gold dashes are a distance guide between the closest ring carbons, not a chemical bond or an electron path. Pale green dashes identify the Tyr2–Leu316 hydrogen-bond contact. Distances use the deposited heavy atoms. Ring angles use least-squares planes through the six ring carbons. Structural resolution and model uncertainty limit their interpretation.

The final bound pose uses 7QVM coordinates. The approach is a rigid, illustrative translation along an outward vector. It is not a molecular-dynamics trajectory, docking search, free-energy calculation or observed entry pathway. Only the bound pose displays contact measurements.
7QVM is an engineered human receptor complex determined by cryo-EM at 3.25 Å. G protein and antibody components are omitted from this view.
The regular phenol ring and peptide attachment cue help explain the tyrosine side chain. They are idealised teaching geometry, with ring hydrogens implicit.
Each aromatic carbon contributes a p orbital perpendicular to the ring plane. The two lobes have opposite wavefunction signs. Their colours do not represent positive and negative electrical charges.

Moving markers guide the explanation. Their number, route and speed are symbolic, not electron counts, electron trajectories or physical timescales. No stimulus or time-dependent calculation is being simulated.
The separate Calculated mode retains the PBE0/def2-SVP fields for the capped Tyr2–Phe291 fragment pair. The teaching geometry does not replace those data.

Stationary single-point electronic model. Orbitals are wavefunctions, not electron trajectories. Orbital signs are not electrical charges. This fragment model does not predict binding affinity or receptor activation.

Results depend on capping, proton orientation, basis and density functional. No time-dependent response or biological validation. The visualization grid undersamples core-density peaks and is not an electron-count integration grid.
